newsitem.title: FINLAND: M-SERLA TO BUY BIBER'S BIBERIST.
newsitem.headline: M-SERLA TO BUY BIBER'S BIBERIST.

text.p: Finnish forest industry group Metsa-Serla Oy said in a statement on Tuesday it will buy Swiss paper maker Biber Holding AG's Biberist fine paper business for less than 300 million markka.
Annual net sales of the Biberist fine paper mill amount to about 1.5 billion markka, Metsa-Serla said.

"Through the acquisition of Biberist, Metsa-Serla will purchase market share in the heart of Europe and in core areas for fine paper and will increase the volume of group fine paper operations to more than one million tonnes per year," it said.
Up to now, Metsa-Serla's fine paper production has totalled 700,000 tonnes per year at three mills in Finland.
Biberist's output capacity is 330,000 tonnes per year. It makes coated and uncoated fine paper. It has been loss-making and Metsa-Serla said rationalisation talks would start at once.
At the same time Metsa-Serla's Finnish partner Myllykoski Oy will buy Biber Holding's Swiss newsprint plant , the output capacity of which is 170,000 tonnes per year, Metsa-Serla said.
The plant, which is located a few km from the Biberist fine paper plant, has a 650 million markka annual net sales and 276 employees, it said.
Sales of Metsa-Serla's sales organisation Metsa-Serla Sales will rise by about two billion markka per year due to the acquisitions, Metsa-Serla said, but did not elaborate.
Biber Holding said in a separate statement it expected to file for bakruptcy once its final balance sheet for 1996 had been worked out and approved by auditors.
Biber said the revenue from the sale of Biberist and Utzenstorf and the company's remaining assets would cover only about 40 percent of its debts.
